column1: # T1 hand-written set (tools/tiamat/TEST_PLAN.md T1): 50 scenarios, written by hand 2026-10-15,
# never used for training. Each line: CLAIM<TAB>A SOURCE THAT SUPPORTS IT (paraphrased)<TAB>
# A SOURCE THAT CONTRADICTS IT (paraphrased)<TAB>A SOURCE ON SOMETHING ELSE.
# make_t1_set.py turns each scenario into four items: TRUE (support + other), FALSE
# (contradiction + other), BOTH (support + contradiction), NEITHER (other only), 200 in all.
# Names are invented so no model can answer from memory.
Orlena Vasq runs the bakery on Tidewater Lane.
column2: The shop register lists Orlena Vasq as owner of the Tidewater Lane bakery.
column3: The register shows the Tidewater Lane bakery has been run by Pell Amoro since it opened, and Orlena Vasq has never worked there.
column4: The harbour office reports that the ferry to Kesh leaves at dawn.

column1: The Quorn footbridge is 48 metres long.
column2: A surveyor measured the Quorn footbridge end to end at forty-eight metres.
column3: The county survey gives the Quorn footbridge a length of 63 metres.
column4: The almanac says the Quorn valley gets heavy rain in March.

column1: Doctor Ilse Brannock teaches chemistry at Halvard College.
column2: Halvard College's staff page names Ilse Brannock as its chemistry lecturer.
column3: Halvard College confirms that Ilse Brannock teaches history there, not chemistry.
column4: A notice says the Halvard library closes early on Fridays.

column1: The Merrow well is 112 metres deep.
column2: Drillers recorded reaching water in the Merrow well at a depth of 112 metres.
column3: The water board lists the Merrow well as 35 metres deep.
column4: The parish newsletter mentions a new bell for the Merrow chapel.

column1: The trawler Silver Juno is owned by Tamsin Ure.
column2: Port records register the Silver Juno to Tamsin Ure.
column3: The port registry shows the Silver Juno belongs to the Ackley fishing cooperative; Tamsin Ure owns no boat.
column4: The harbour master notes that the north pier is being repainted.

column1: The Dovecote market has 140 stalls.
column2: The market charter allows for and fills exactly 140 stalls at Dovecote.
column3: The town clerk counted 86 stalls at the Dovecote market.
column4: The weather station logged a frost at Dovecote on Tuesday.

column1: Rasmus Kell was born in the village of Ferrant.
column2: Ferrant's parish register records the birth of Rasmus Kell.
column3: Rasmus Kell's birth certificate gives his birthplace as Oldmere, far from Ferrant.
column4: The census lists Ferrant's population as just under nine hundred.

column1: The Greywick archive holds 9,300 scrolls.
column2: The archivist's inventory totals 9,300 scrolls at Greywick.
column3: The latest audit found only 2,150 scrolls in the Greywick archive.
column4: The courier reports a new road being laid towards Greywick.

column1: Lina Osgood works for the Saltmarsh shipping guild.
column2: The Saltmarsh guild's payroll includes Lina Osgood.
column3: The guild states Lina Osgood left Saltmarsh years ago and now works for a mill in Brent.
column4: The guild's newsletter announces a summer fair.

column1: The Calder tunnel opened in 1911.
column2: Engineering records show the Calder tunnel opening to traffic in 1911.
column3: A plaque at the Calder tunnel gives its opening year as 1934.
column4: The rail timetable lists six trains a day through Calder junction.

column1: Mira Toller is the mayor of Elsby.
column2: The Elsby council minutes are signed by Mayor Mira Toller.
column3: Elsby's council says its mayor is Harlan Fisk; Mira Toller is the town's treasurer.
column4: The Elsby gazette reports a record apple harvest.

column1: The Hesketh reservoir holds 4 million cubic metres of water.
column2: The water authority rates the Hesketh reservoir at four million cubic metres.
column3: According to the authority, Hesketh holds 11 million cubic metres when full.
column4: A ranger reports otters returning to the Hesketh stream.

column1: The lighthouse at Corran Point is painted red and white.
column2: Sailors describe the Corran Point lighthouse by its red and white bands.
column3: The maritime guide says the Corran Point lighthouse is plain white with a black lantern.
column4: The tide table lists high water at Corran at 4:10.

column1: Bertil Noake owns the orchard at Little Fennick.
column2: Land deeds name Bertil Noake as the holder of the Little Fennick orchard.
column3: The deeds show the Little Fennick orchard belongs to the Pryor family; Bertil Noake rents a cottage nearby.
column4: The parish notes a fox seen near the Fennick road.

column1: The Amberly choir has 32 members.
column2: The choir's roll lists thirty-two singers at Amberly.
column3: The Amberly choirmaster says the choir has 18 members this season.
column4: The Amberly hall is booked for a dance on Saturday.

column1: Professor Hale Durand lives in the town of Wickmoor.
column2: The electoral roll for Wickmoor includes Hale Durand.
column3: Hale Durand's address on file is in Ashgrove; he has never lived in Wickmoor.
column4: The Wickmoor bus timetable changed last month.

column1: The Pellam mine produced 2,400 tonnes of tin last year.
column2: The mine's annual report states 2,400 tonnes of tin were raised at Pellam.
column3: The trade ministry recorded only 600 tonnes of tin from Pellam last year.
column4: The miners' club elected a new chairman.

column1: The ferry Lark crosses to Isle Morrow in forty minutes.
column2: The ferry company times the Lark's crossing to Isle Morrow at forty minutes.
column3: Passengers are told the Lark takes two hours to reach Isle Morrow.
column4: The Isle Morrow museum reopens in spring.

column1: Gretchen Albray was born in the town of Haverlund.
column2: A birth notice in the Haverlund paper announces Gretchen Albray's arrival.
column3: Gretchen Albray was born at sea, on a ship bound for Coldharbour, records say.
column4: The Haverlund census shows many families keep goats.

column1: The Ninefield road is 27 kilometres long.
column2: The highways board lists the Ninefield road at 27 kilometres.
column3: Cyclists measure the Ninefield road at 54 kilometres, and the board agrees with them.
column4: A farm on the Ninefield road sells honey.

column1: Ivo Penhallow works as a clockmaker in Strand Cross.
column2: Strand Cross trade listings show Ivo Penhallow, clockmaker.
column3: Ivo Penhallow is a ferryman at Strand Cross and has never repaired clocks.
column4: The Strand Cross church clock was cleaned this year.

column1: The Brightwater school has 410 pupils.
column2: The headteacher's report counts 410 pupils on the Brightwater roll.
column3: The education office lists Brightwater school with 190 pupils.
column4: The school's football team won its league.

column1: Annika Roe owns a boat named Petrel.
column2: The mooring list gives the Petrel to Annika Roe.
column3: Annika Roe has never owned a boat; the Petrel belongs to the sailing club.
column4: The sailing club's regatta is in August.

column1: The Thornbury viaduct has 21 arches.
column2: A guidebook counts twenty-one arches on the Thornbury viaduct.
column3: Engineers report the Thornbury viaduct stands on 14 arches.
column4: The Thornbury station café serves breakfast until ten.

column1: Cassius Wren teaches music at the Lowgate academy.
column2: The Lowgate academy lists Cassius Wren as its music teacher.
column3: Cassius Wren teaches mathematics at Lowgate, and the academy has no music teacher this year.
column4: The academy's roof was repaired over the winter.

column1: The village of Eskdale Minor has one bakery.
column2: Locals say Eskdale Minor's only bakery is on the green.
column3: The trade register lists three bakeries in Eskdale Minor.
column4: The Eskdale Minor fete raised money for the church.

column1: The Harrow dam was finished in 1958.
column2: The dam's builders completed the Harrow dam in 1958, the record says.
column3: The Harrow dam was finished in 1972, according to the water board.
column4: Anglers report good trout below the Harrow dam.

column1: Selma Prack is the head of the Riverside hospital.
column2: The Riverside hospital board names Selma Prack as its director.
column3: Riverside's director is Doctor Okafor; Selma Prack is a nurse on the night ward.
column4: The hospital garden won a prize for its roses.

column1: The Kittering clock tower is 36 metres tall.
column2: The tower's architect gave the Kittering clock tower a height of thirty-six metres.
column3: A recent survey measured the Kittering clock tower at 22 metres.
column4: The clock in the tower strikes every quarter hour.

column1: Joran Mallet was born in the city of Port Vessel.
column2: Port Vessel's records hold the birth entry of Joran Mallet.
column3: Joran Mallet's papers show he was born inland, in Dray, and moved to Port Vessel as a child.
column4: Port Vessel's harbour handles grain and timber.

column1: The Oakhurst library lends 5,000 books a month.
column2: The librarian reports about five thousand loans each month at Oakhurst.
column3: Lending at Oakhurst averages 800 books a month, says the council.
column4: The Oakhurst library has a new reading room for children.

column1: Tobias Grail works for the Northmoor railway company.
column2: Northmoor railway staff lists include Tobias Grail, signalman.
column3: Tobias Grail works for a bank in Lisk; the railway has no record of him.
column4: The Northmoor line is closed for repairs on Sunday.

column1: The Sandby beach is 3 kilometres long.
column2: The coast guide gives Sandby beach a length of three kilometres.
column3: The Sandby tourist office says the beach stretches for 9 kilometres.
column4: A café at Sandby sells crab sandwiches.

column1: The painter Odile Faraway lives in the hamlet of Crossley.
column2: Crossley's residents' list includes the painter Odile Faraway.
column3: Odile Faraway lives in the capital and has only visited Crossley once.
column4: Crossley's pond froze over in January.

column1: The Dunmore lifeboat crew has 24 volunteers.
column2: The lifeboat station counts twenty-four volunteers at Dunmore.
column3: The Dunmore station says its crew is down to 11 volunteers.
column4: A storm warning was issued for the Dunmore coast.

column1: The Ashcombe mill grinds wheat.
column2: The miller at Ashcombe grinds wheat into flour every week.
column3: The Ashcombe mill has ground only barley since it was built, the miller says.
column4: A heron nests by the Ashcombe millpond.

column1: Leander Fosk owns the hardware shop in Moorgate.
column2: The Moorgate trade register lists Leander Fosk as owner of the hardware shop.
column3: The Moorgate hardware shop is owned by the Quill brothers; Leander Fosk is their delivery driver.
column4: Moorgate's market is held on Thursdays.

column1: The Ellery canal has 17 locks.
column2: The canal trust counts seventeen locks along the Ellery canal.
column3: Boaters' maps show the Ellery canal with 29 locks.
column4: The canal towpath is popular with walkers.

column1: Dagny Hollis teaches geography at Bramble school.
column2: Bramble school's timetable shows Dagny Hollis teaching geography.
column3: Dagny Hollis teaches art at Bramble, the school confirms, not geography.
column4: Bramble school's sports day is in June.

column1: The Westgate theatre seats 650 people.
column2: The theatre's plans show 650 seats in the Westgate auditorium.
column3: The fire inspector capped the Westgate theatre at 300 seats, its full capacity.
column4: The Westgate theatre's next play is a comedy.

column1: The village of Upper Brinn was founded in 1702.
column2: The founding charter of Upper Brinn is dated 1702.
column3: Historians date the founding of Upper Brinn to 1840.
column4: Upper Brinn hosts a sheepdog trial every autumn.

column1: Rufus Ainsley works for the Coldwater weather bureau.
column2: The Coldwater bureau's roster includes forecaster Rufus Ainsley.
column3: Rufus Ainsley works at the Coldwater post office; the bureau has no such forecaster.
column4: The bureau predicts a dry week ahead.

column1: The Fenwick orchard has 380 apple trees.
column2: The orchard keeper counted 380 apple trees at Fenwick.
column3: A survey of the Fenwick orchard found 95 apple trees.
column4: The Fenwick cider press is a hundred years old.

column1: Marguerite Solano was born in the village of Caddis.
column2: Caddis's chapel register records the baptism of Marguerite Solano.
column3: Marguerite Solano was born in Velloran, across the border, her passport says.
column4: Caddis is known for its wool.

column1: The Highcliff funicular climbs 140 metres.
column2: The funicular company states a climb of 140 metres at Highcliff.
column3: The engineers' plate on the Highcliff funicular gives a rise of 60 metres.
column4: The Highcliff funicular runs every twenty minutes.

column1: Pieter Vance is the captain of the steamer Albatross.
column2: The Albatross's crew list names Pieter Vance as captain.
column3: The Albatross is captained by Moira Lund; Pieter Vance is its cook.
column4: The Albatross sails to the islands on Mondays.

column1: The Rookwood forest covers 70 square kilometres.
column2: The forestry office gives Rookwood forest an area of seventy square kilometres.
column3: The map office measures Rookwood forest at 12 square kilometres.
column4: Deer are often seen at the edge of Rookwood.

column1: Helga Strom owns the inn at Ravensgate.
column2: The Ravensgate licensing book names Helga Strom as the innkeeper and owner.
column3: The Ravensgate inn belongs to the brewery; Helga Strom only manages the kitchen.
column4: The inn at Ravensgate has six rooms.

column1: The Pellingham bell weighs 900 kilograms.
column2: The bell foundry's record gives the Pellingham bell a weight of 900 kilograms.
column3: When it was rehung, the Pellingham bell weighed in at 2,300 kilograms.
column4: The bell is rung for weddings and on New Year's Eve.

column1: Osric Thale works as a ranger in the Blackfen reserve.
column2: The Blackfen reserve staff list includes ranger Osric Thale.
column3: Osric Thale is a teacher in Blackfen town and has never worked at the reserve.
column4: The Blackfen reserve is home to rare orchids.
